newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to tender for 100,000T soy, 8,000T corn.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to tender for 100,000T soy, 8,000T corn.

text.p: Taiwanese buyers will probably tender for up to 100,000 tonnes of soybeans and 8,000 tonnes of corn next week, traders said on Friday.
Oilseed buyers are likely to shift their attention to South American soybeans and away from U.S. origins as their prices are seen to be more attractive, the dealers said.
"South American beans simply have better prices with acceptable qualities," Hui Shung Group buyer Jack Lee said.
Taiwan has bought a total of 146,000 tonnes of Brazilian soybeans since the beginning of May and will seek the additional 100,000 tonnes over the next two weeks, traders said.
The Hui Shung Group will retender for a shipment of 46,000 tonnes of soybeans and 8,000 tonnes of corn, they said.
The Group passed on a tender on Thursday. The lowest Brazilian soybean quote reached 171 U.S. cents per tonne over September Chicago futures, or about US$324.50 a tonne C&F.
The lowest U.S. soybean quote was seen at 189 U.S. cents a tonne over September Chicago futures, or about $331 a tonne.
The Taichung division of Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association may also tender soon for a 54,000-tonne soybean shipment, traders said.
Almost all of the soybeans bought by Taiwan used to come from the United States.
Taiwan is not expected to buy any wheat next week.
Freight rates from the U.S. Pacific Northwest were quoted at about $11.00 a tonne while rates from the Gulf of Mexico reached $21.00 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized June shipments.
